column1: # What each display-generator request does, one line each (older rows are five words or fewer), written by hand from the handler readings
# in ucode/arm1_functions.md (arm1.u, IRIX 6.5.30m). scripts/dg_requests.py joins it with DGDispatchTable.

column2: reads payload word 0, adds one and sends the sum back as a one-word reply, a loop-back check of the command path that touches no hardware
writes payload word 1 to the display-bus word indexed by payload word 0, ARM address 0x600000 plus four times the index, between short delay loops and with no range check
writes 0 to XMAP register 0x105, which turns the diagnostic substitute colour off, between delay loops and then forces an XMAP copy-buffer update; reads no payload
prints a message that bus tracing was not compiled in and returns; it ignores its four payload words and touches no hardware
stores payload word 0 as the firmware debug-print mask in the first word of the display state and prints the new value; no hardware access and no reply
read-modify-writes bits 21-20 of display-bus register 0x8b with the low two bits of payload word 0, which pick the input sync source; sends no reply
replies with the horizontal phase last stored for the channel named by payload word 0, the word at channel record offset 0x16c, as a four-byte reply of type 3

decodes payload word 0 as a signed vertical phase with the channel number plus one in its top ten bits; it stores the value in the shared slot for all channels or channel 1, or in the channel record at offset 0x168, and applies it through the vertical-phase adjuster
replies with the vertical phase last stored, the shared slot at display-state offset 0x36cc for channel 1 and otherwise the channel record word at offset 0x168, as a four-byte reply of type 4

sets bit 25 of the channel control word when payload word 1 is -2, meaning no gamma map; any other value clears the bit and stores the map index at record offset 0x170, then XMAP channel-format register 0x11d is updated
replies with the gamma-map index at record offset 0x170 of the channel named by payload word 0, as a four-byte reply of type 5, without a range check on the channel
builds the five-word board-configuration record on the stack through the configuration reader and sends it as a 20-byte reply of type 6; reads no hardware itself
calls the channel resize routine with the eight payload words; when other channels copy this one (record offset 0xbc above zero) it applies the same resize to every dependent channel
replies with 18 words of the channel resize state, the record words 0x50-0x6f and the placement words and bits 23 and 22 of the control word at offset 0x184, as a 72-byte reply of type 8
hands the 16-word payload to the per-channel genlock-parameter writer for every present video-output chip; it is a tail call with no hardware access of its own
combines the 13-bit horizontal position in payload word 0 with the vertical position in word 1 shifted into bits 25-13 and writes the result to XMAP cursor register 0x102
looks up the channel record named by payload word 0 and writes its first word, the channel index, to XMAP register 0x100, choosing which channel owns the hardware cursor
writes XMAP register 0x103 with 2 for payload value zero and 1 for payload value one; any other value writes zero, cursor off, and no state is kept
replies with the channel blank bit, bit 31 of the record control word at offset 0x184, or with 1 when the shared blanking-depth word at display-state offset 0x36d0 is above zero
replies with the output gain: for channel 1 with bit 26 of its control word set the shared word at display-state offset 0x36bc, otherwise the record word at offset 0x15c
reads video-DAC control register 6 for a channel numbered 0-7 and replies with its bit 3, the pedestal enable, or with -1 for any other channel number
replies with two words from the record control word at offset 0x184: first bit 28, the enabled flag, then bit 27, as an eight-byte reply of type 0x13
replies with bit 9 of the channel record word at offset 0x88, the field-dominance flag, as a four-byte reply of type 0x15
replies with bit 27 of the display status word at 0x0406cd1c, the internal genlock flag, as a four-byte reply of type 0x1c
replies with two words, bit 21 of the record control word at offset 0x184 and then the record word at offset 0x180, as an eight-byte reply of type 0x1d
